title: Pinch-zoom a street map on a loose tablet until the whole red walking route fits on the screen
keywords: tablet, touchscreen, pinch to zoom, two-finger gesture, map, route, multi-touch, light contact, fingertip, everyday
instruction: Zoom the map out until the whole red route fits on the screen, filling at least half its width, then lift your fingers off.
context: Pinching two fingers together to zoom a map out is something most adults do daily on a phone or tablet, and a home robot showing someone a route, photo or document has to do it too. Physically it is unforgiving: both fingertips must land on the glass of a loose 434 g tablet together and level, within a fraction of a millimetre, and stay touching under a light press while they slide toward each other. A fingertip that lands alone and drifts more than about 1.4 mm drags the map sideways instead of zooming; a still, quick touch on a place pin opens a card that covers the map; two quick taps zoom in. The map zooms by the ratio of the fingers' end and start spacing, about the point between them, so where the fingers land and how far they close decide whether the route ends up on the screen: landing 90 mm apart, they must end 16 to 31 mm apart, about a point within a few centimetres of the right one.
setup: Metres; x forward from the line through the arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up from the desk top; arm bases at (0, +0.305) and (0, -0.305). (1) Tablet, loose, no case: Amazon Fire HD 10 (2023), 246 x 164.8 x 8.6 mm, 434 g, black, screen up in landscape, long side along y, centred at (0.200, -0.060) on a laminate desk (back on desk friction about 0.4, estimate). Its 10.1-inch 1920 x 1200 screen shows a 217.6 x 136.0 mm picture centred on the front; picture right is the robot's right (-y), picture top is away from the robot (+x). Kept awake, full screen. (2) On the screen: the page map.html from the task folder, a street map drawn by the open-source web map library Leaflet 1.9.4 (our own synthetic street plan: grey-beige blocks, white streets, orange main roads, a river, parks), touch pinch-zoom on, no inertia, no zoom animation, no rotation, zoom limits 1/8x to 4x of the start. A red walking route 3 mm wide runs along the streets from a green start disc to a dark end disc. At the start the route's bounding box is 600 x 300 mm on the screen (2.8 screen widths), centred 20 mm right of the screen centre, so only its middle shows. Three blue place pins (7 mm discs) sit off the route: a cafe 60 mm left of and 37 mm above the screen centre, a museum 70 mm right and 40 mm below, a pharmacy off screen; tapping a pin opens its 44 x 24 mm white place card. A pinch along the screen's middle line passes 30 mm or more from the pins. (3) Robot fingertips: for the real trial each finger's 15 x 4 mm end face is wrapped in conductive fabric tape (or carries a conductive stylus nib) wired to the robot's grounded frame, so the capacitive screen registers it; in simulation a fingertip touches the screen when its end face rests on the glass (within 0.2 mm). Nothing else on the desk. Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. Reach: the screen centre is 0.33 m from the right arm base.
scoring: Read from the viewer's state every 50 ms step (in the real trial, from a screen recording synchronised with the trial video). FITS: the route's bounding box lies wholly on the screen at least 5 mm inside every edge, and is at least 108.8 mm (half the screen) wide; with this route that means a zoom of 0.18x to 0.35x of the start, about the right place. The map can only zoom out by pinching (no zoom buttons; a double tap zooms in), so any credit for zooming out needs a pinch. PINCH: two touches on the glass together whose spacing fell to 75% or less of its start. SETTLED: no fingertip on the glass, every fingertip 20 mm or more above the glass or 10 mm or more outside the tablet's outline, and the tablet still (under 0.5 mm per step), all for 1 s. Score at the end: 1.0 settled, FITS, no place card open, and the tablet within 20 mm of its start, turned under 5 degrees and flat (success when this holds 1 s more); 0.75 settled and FITS but a card open or the tablet moved or turned; 0.5 settled and zoomed out to 0.5x or less (including too far: the 1/8x limit leaves the route 75 mm wide) but not FITS; 0.25 a PINCH happened at any time; 0 otherwise. Zero for the whole trial: the tablet turned over (over 45 degrees) or off the desk (20 mm below its top), the screen cracked, or a touch landing within 3 mm of a screen edge (an edge swipe can leave the map).
run_limit: 800 steps (40 s at 20 Hz), about 2.7x the scripted demo's 14.9 s (298 steps; it succeeds at step 222)
reset_notes: Reload map.html (it always opens at the start view, card closed) and tap its overlay to go full screen; lay the tablet back on its tape marks; ready pose, grippers open.
fidelity: Tablet: one rigid body, one material for back and glass (friction 0.4/0.35, estimate). The task redraws the screen every 50 ms from the touches with Leaflet 1.9.4's touch rules (matched against Leaflet in Chromium with emulated touches). Touch is the end face resting on the glass (within 0.2 mm), not capacitive sensing; touches sampled at 20 Hz (panel: 120 Hz). CSS pixel 0.17 mm (estimate). Synthetic map without labels, as in the real trial. Touches under 12 mm apart are not merged.
